       1             SENATOR MAZIARZ:  Good morning, everyone.

       2             It is about ten after ten, and we're going to

       3      get started.

       4             I'm Senator George Maziarz, Chairman of the

       5      Senate Select Committee on State-Native American

       6      Relations.

       7             I would like to call this inaugural meeting

       8      of the Senate Select Committee to order.

       9             This is, I think, a very historic event.  It

      10      marks the first official meeting of the first-ever

      11      legislative committee on this very important issue.

      12             Let me begin by thanking my colleagues,

      13      Senator Tim Kennedy, and Senator Pat Gallivan, for

      14      being here today, and for being very supportive of

      15      the mission of this Committee.

      16             I also want to thank the Native American

      17      nations for their cooperation and support of this

      18      committee since it was formed this past June.

      19             There are nine nations that are officially

      20      recognized by the State of New York.  They are as

      21      follows:  The Cayugas, the Oneidas, the Onondagas,

      22      the Mohawks, the Senecas, the Shinnecocks, the

      23      Tonawanda Band of Senecas, the Tuscarora, and

      24      the Unkechauge.

      25             Each of these nations has a unique history





 

                                                                   4
       1      and culture, and they are a vital part of the

       2      economy and social fabric of our state.

       3             This committee was formed in order to correct

       4      a wrong that has existed in this state for far too

       5      long; namely, the fact that there was no official

       6      State forum to discuss Native American issues,

       7      listen to their concerns, offer legislation, and

       8      promote cooperation and real solutions.

       9             There are currently about

      10      106,000 Native Americans living in New York State,

      11      with over 32,000 living on native lands.  New York

      12      currently ranks ninth in terms of native population

      13      among all of the states.

      14             As a result of the large population of

      15      Native Americans in our state, and the large.

      16             Effect that these nations have on New York

      17      State economy, I believe there is a definite need

      18      for this Committee.

      19             Our mission statement for this Committee is:

      20             To enable members of the State Senate to

      21      become informed and educated about the Indian

      22      nations located here in New York;

      23             And, to establish a formal avenue for

      24      dialogue between State-elected officials and native

      25      peoples;





 

                                                                   5
       1             And, to improve understanding and cooperation

       2      between the State and those native peoples.

       3             Today we take the first step in accomplishing

       4      our mission.  We will focus on three main goals.

       5             First:  Allowing each of the Native American

       6      nations who are in attendance today to address the

       7      Committee, and provide a brief overview of their

       8      history and culture;

       9             Second:  We have asked each to provide an

      10      overview of their current economic development

      11      activities, and their impact on the economy of each

      12      nation, as well as upon the State of New York, and

      13      the area of the state that they are located;

      14             Lastly:  We will hear about new economic

      15      development projects that are under consideration by

      16      each nation, and discuss potential partnerships with

      17      the State of New York.

      18             In short, we are here to promote

      19      understanding and cooperation.  Everyone here knows

      20      that our economy is struggling now, and we need to

      21      do all that we can to get it back on track.

      22             The economic impact of the activities that

      23      native nations have makes them some of the largest

      24      employers in our state.  Therefore, it is more

      25      important now than it ever has been, to promote





 

                                                                   6
       1      economic-development partnerships to create jobs for

       2      our citizens, and for sovereign native peoples as

       3      well.

       4             Today we will hear from the leaders of

       5      several Native American nations.

       6             I want to welcome:  Chairman Richard Nephew,

       7      the Seneca Nation Council;

       8             Dave Kimelberg, the CEO of Seneca Holdings;

       9             Representative Ray Halbritter, of the

      10      Oneida Indian Nation;

      11             Chief Ron LaFrance, Jr., of the

      12      Saint Regis Mohawk Indian Nation;

      13             And, Chairman Randy King, of the

      14      Shinnecock Indian Nation.

      15             I would ask that each speaker try to confine

      16      their presentation to 15 minutes.  And, following

      17      each presentation, we will allow the members of this

      18      Committee to ask any questions.

      19             Thank you very much.

      20             I would just also like to note for the

      21      record, that several of the members of this

      22      Committee, Senator Ruth Hassell-Thompson, has

      23      staff -- senior staff in attendance, as does

      24      Senator John DeFrancisco.

      25             And, with that, I will ask my colleagues if





 

                                                                   7
       1      they would care to make some sort of an opening

       2      statement.

       3             Senator Gallivan.

       4             SENATOR GALLIVAN:  Thank you, Chairman.

       5             Good morning, everybody.

       6             I too believe that there is a need for this

       7      Committee.  It's kind of amazing that nothing like

       8      this has taken place for all of these years, that,

       9      the Indian nations and New York State residents have

      10      co-existed within our boundaries.

      11             I view this as a mechanism to facilitate

      12      discussions between the State, the Indian nations

      13      and tribal leaders, on issues in which the State and

      14      Indian nations and tribes share our common interest

      15      or jurisdiction.

      16             I would like to welcome all of you here to

      17      Albany.  I look forward to hearing the testimony

      18      from the different nations.  And, I certainly look

      19      forward to advancing our common interests, and

      20      moving this state and our relationships forward.

      21             Thank you.

      22             SENATOR MAZIARZ:  Thank you, Senator.

      23             Senator Kennedy.

      24             SENATOR KENNEDY:  Thank you very much.

      25             Good morning.





 

                                                                   8
       1             This is a historic occasion, that this

       2      meeting is taking place today.

       3             New York State has a long history of

       4      cooperation with the Seneca Nation in

       5      Western New York, and all of our Native American

       6      tribes.

       7             I'm proud to be a part of this new State

       8      recognition of that cooperation, as we hold the

       9      first public hearing of the Senate Standing

      10      Committee on State-Native American Relations.

      11             Our history intertwines and our cultures

      12      overlap, and that adds to the rich cultural history

      13      of Western New York, and in New York State.  And it

      14      provides an important boost as we continue to build

      15      on the collaboration and cooperation that has

      16      benefited our state.

      17             In Western New York, the Seneca Nation is an

      18      important contributor to our regional economy.  This

      19      path of economic cooperation shared between

      20      Western New York and the Seneca Nation stretches

      21      years and years in the past.

      22             Through this economic cooperation, we have

      23      already accomplished some great things, and

      24      continued cooperation will help advance our

      25      collective goal of revitalizing the Western New York





 

                                                                   9
       1      economy.

       2             The Senate Standing Committee on

       3      Native American Relations presents an opportunity

       4      for us to foster an open dialogue, which is

       5      essential to our future relationships with our state

       6      Native American tribes.  And it is this open

       7      dialogue that will help our state and the

       8      Native American tribes mend and strengthen the bonds

       9      that run between us.

      10             I was pleased to learn about recent meetings

      11      between representatives of the Cuomo Administration

      12      and representatives of the Seneca Nation of Indians,

      13      including President Robert Odawi Porter.

      14             A productive and consistent dialogue between

      15      New York State and the Seneca Nation of Indians is

      16      important to both parties.  And I am hopeful it will

      17      help to resolve many of the outstanding issues

      18      facing both the Seneca Nation and New York State.

      19             I expect this Committee to foster that

      20      communication.

      21             And, I'm sure it will, with the

      22      great Chairman.

      23             SENATOR MAZIARZ:  Thank you, Senator.

      24             I've also been told that we have some

      25      senior staff from Senator Little's office here,





 

                                                                   10
       1      also.

       2             With that, we will ask our first witness,

       3      Chairman Richard Nephew, of the Seneca Nation

       4      Council; and, Dave Kimelberg, CEO of Seneca Holding

       5      Company.

       6             Chairman Nephew, and CEO Kimelberg.

       7             Thank you very much for being here today.

       8             Senator Young is also represented here today.

       9             Richard.

      10             RICHARD NEPHEW:  Thank you.

      11             Good morning.

      12                  [Speaks in native language.]

      13             What I just said in the Seneca language is,

      14      that, I'm thankful that all are well here today, and

      15      that you're able to be here, and meet with us,

      16      everyone here in the room.

      17             This is a very historic meeting, and I'm

      18      honored to represent the Seneca Nation, and be here

      19      to testify before your Committee.

      20             And, I would like to thank, Senator Maziarz,

      21      and colleagues, for forming this very important

      22      committee.

      23             I think we all realize that conflict is much

      24      more costly than cooperation.  And, we hope this is

      25      a very positive step forward, as we move forward,





 

                                                                   11
       1      and do what's best for Western New York and

       2      New York State and the Seneca Nation.

       3             I believe 15 minutes is far too short, but,

       4      we'll do our best here.  And, in the interest of

       5      time and accuracy, I'll read my statement now.

       6             I'll be glad to elaborate on it, on anything,

       7      later on.

       8             My name is Richard Nephew, and I serve as

       9      chairman of the Seneca Nation Council.  And I'm

      10      joined here, by Dave Kimelberg, chief executive

      11      officer of Seneca Holdings.

      12             I'm going to briefly provide you with

      13      information about the Seneca Nation, and our

      14      history, and of our dealings with New York State.

      15             David will then speak about the

      16      Seneca Nation's economic enterprises and our

      17      regional impact.

      18             Today's committee hearing is a historic

      19      event.  I applaud your efforts, Senator Maziarz, in

      20      creating this committee.

      21             I too believe there is an urgent need for a

      22      productive dialogue between the State of New York,

      23      and the Indian nations and tribes located within the

      24      state's boundaries.

      25             For too long, the State has attempted to make





 

                                                                   12
       1      decisions that impact the Seneca Nation, and other

       2      native peoples, without having an adequate

       3      understanding of our history and our culture, and of

       4      our sovereign treaty rights.

       5             Let us hope that this is the beginning of a

       6      long and productive dialogue that will benefit my

       7      people and yours.

       8             I also believe that it is important that you

       9      have chosen to have economic development as the

      10      topic of the Select Committee's first hearing.

      11             As you know, the Western New York economy has

      12      long been in decline.  People and families are

      13      suffering, and job creation is sorely needed.

      14      Leadership is sorely needed.

      15             For more than a thousand years, the

      16      Seneca people have lived in what is now known as

      17      "Western New York."  We have witnessed, experienced,

      18      and endured many changes over the centuries.  And

      19      today we are a proud nation, with a rich history

      20      and -- rich culture, and a promising future.

      21             The Seneca Nation of Indians is the largest

      22      of six indigenous nations that comprise

      23      The Six Nations Haudenosaunee Confederacy, also

      24      known as "Iroquois."

      25             Following the American Revolutionary War, we





 

                                                                   13
       1      lost most of our aboriginal lands in a

       2      land-for-peace deal that secured the title to the

       3      lands we now occupy.

       4             Most of our 8,000 citizens live on or near

       5      our Allegheny and Cattaraugus territories in

       6      Western New York.

       7             Combined with our Oil Springs, Buffalo Creek,

       8      and Niagara Falls territories, we own, and retain

       9      full jurisdiction, of over 50,000 acres.

      10             In 1794, the Seneca Nation, along with other

      11      nations of The Six Nations Haudenosaunee

      12      Confederacy, signed a treaty with the newly

      13      established United States of America, recognizing

      14      the sovereignty of the Seneca Nation, and

      15      establishing peace between our nations.

      16             We were promised, in the Canandaigua treaty

      17      of 1794, that we would forever be secure in the free

      18      use and enjoyment of our lands.

      19             There have been many challenges in our

      20      relationship during the last 216 years, but our

      21      treaty relationship with the United States continues

      22      today.

      23             The United States recently fulfilled one of

      24      its obligations under the Canandaigua treaty by

      25      sending our share of $4,500 worth of cloth that is





 

                                                                   14
       1      distributed annually to the Haudenosaunee people.

       2             Unfortunately, many of the promises made to

       3      us by the United States have either remained

       4      unfulfilled or have been broken, particularly the

       5      obligation to protect our nation from the predatory

       6      behavior of New York State, and its officials, over

       7      many years.

       8             In the last two centuries, the Seneca Nation

       9      has had to deal with repeated efforts by the State

      10      to take over our lands, to impose taxation, commerce

      11      on our lands, and even to take control over our

      12      children to educate them.

      13             For many years, our very identity as a

      14      distinct indigenous people was threatened.

      15             Let me share some recent history.

      16             In 1954, New York State pressured us into

      17      signing an illegal right-of-way agreement, to enable

      18      the New York State Thruway to cross our Cattaraugus

      19      territory near Silver Creek, for which we received

      20      inadequate compensation.

      21             In 1961, New York State actively supported

      22      the taking of 10,000 acres of our

      23      Allegheny territory, by the United States, for the

      24      Allegheny Reservoir and the Kinzua Dam.

      25             In 1976, the State coerced us into allowing





 

                                                                   15
       1      the Southern Tier Expressway to cross our

       2      Allegheny territory, by making promises, to this day

       3      remain unfulfilled.

       4             And, now, New York State is breaking its

       5      promise of gaming-machine exclusivity that it made

       6      to the Seneca Nation in 2002, when we entered into a

       7      gaming compact, by allowing casino-like machines,

       8      and marketing them, in racinos, now called

       9      "casinos," and discussing adoption of a

      10      constitutional amendment that would allow

      11      commercialized gaming near our existing facilities

      12      and our promised exclusivity zone.

      13             Despite these repeated challenges, we refuse

      14      to relinquish our treaty-protected guarantees for

      15      political and economic sovereignty.

      16             We continue to look ahead to see what

      17      opportunities lie ahead of us.

      18             There is much for the Seneca Nation to be

      19      proud of in terms of our economy.

      20             In a short period of time, we have made

      21      ourselves into the fifth largest employer in

      22      Western New York, supplying nearly 6,000 high-paying

      23      jobs, with full benefits.

      24             We invested over -- somewhere near

      25      900 million in construction projects over the last





 

                                                                   16
       1      9 years.

       2             We operate a 1. billion economy through your

       3      government, public and private-sector ventures, and

       4      our economic benefit stay in Western New York.  They

       5      are not paid out to stockholders around the country,

       6      or around the world.

       7             Our future is here.  We have committed to

       8      investing in Western New York, and an interest in

       9      seeing the area economy grow and improve.

      10             Every Friday, the payroll of the

      11      Seneca Nation and our gaming enterprises contributes

      12      to the Western New York economy.  We give

      13      New York State an economic shot in the arm every

      14      Friday.  Those dollars circulate in

      15      Western New York, and for the most part, stay in the

      16      region.

      17             Seneca Nation has recently begun a

      18      long-term effort to diversify our economy.

      19             We understand that tobacco and gaming are not

      20      future-growth industry we can rely on solely.  We

      21      also recognize that we are not an island.

      22             That is why, this past June, the

      23      Seneca Nation of Indians invited a number of

      24      public-sector and quasi-public-sector economic

      25      development groups, from Western New York and





 

                                                                   17
       1      Pennsylvania, to discuss how we can work

       2      collaboratively.

       3             We recognize the outreach, and we recognize

       4      that outreach and collaboration are the keys to

       5      success.

       6             The Seneca Nation of Indians is committed to

       7      continuing our role as a significant catalyst for

       8      economic growth in the region.  A financially and

       9      economically vibrant Seneca Nation of Indians will

      10      benefit the region as a whole.

      11             It is our hope that we can find the right

      12      partners who can help us advance the right strategy.

      13             And, in partners, you know, we hope that this

      14      Committee, and all branches of the New York State

      15      government, will also be those partners.

      16             We have been here for a very long time, and

      17      we're always going to be here.  We're not going

      18      anywhere.  We don't have the luxury, or the -- even

      19      the opportunity, to move out of state, to move to

      20      another country, to develop our economic engines

      21      that we need to develop and strategize for our

      22      future.

      23             We don't have that luxury to move away.

      24             We're always gonna here.  And, we know that

      25      we need to reach out to, our neighbors, our





 

                                                                   18
       1      partners, in New York State, and develop that

       2      winning partnership.

       3             As I said at the beginning, conflict is

       4      always much more expensive than cooperation, and,

       5      we're looking for that, moving into the future.

       6             I'll now ask David Kimelberg, chief executive

       7      officer of Seneca Holdings, to provide some detailed

       8      information about the Seneca Nation's economy, and

       9      our efforts to grow and diversify our economic

      10      interests.

      11             DAVID KIMELBERG:  Thank you, Richard.

      12                  [Speaks in native language.]

      13             Good morning, Senator Maziarz, and members of

      14      the Select Committee.

      15             Like Chairman Nephew, I'm pleased to have the

      16      opportunity to speak with you today.

      17             My name is David Kimelberg.  I am a citizen

      18      of the Seneca Nation, and the chief executive

      19      officer of Seneca Holdings, which is the

      20      Seneca Nation's private equity investment and

      21      holding company.

      22             I returned to the Seneca Nation two years

      23      ago, after over a decade of working in the

      24      private equity and venture capital investment

      25      industries.





 

                                                                   19
       1             I came back to serve the Seneca Nation, and

       2      to help execute on what I saw as a tremendous

       3      opportunity to build and diversify the

       4      Seneca Nation's economy.

       5             Two years later, we have accomplished far

       6      more than I expected.  And, I anticipate that this

       7      success will continue to grow rapidly.

       8             The Seneca Nation's largely known for its

       9      gaming and tobacco industries.  These industries, as

      10      Chairman Nephew has indicated, have created enormous

      11      amounts of revenue and jobs in the Western New York

      12      region.

      13             I just wanted to underscore that.

      14             We have created an over $1 billion a year

      15      economy, and we're the fifth largest employer in

      16      Western New York, which came very fast.

      17             What may not be as widely known, is that the

      18      Seneca Nation's economy is rapidly evolving, to

      19      include a diverse number of other industries.

      20             Seneca Holdings, the company that I lead, is

      21      leading that charge with great success, and I'd like

      22      to share some of that with you.

      23             The Seneca Nation established Seneca Holdings

      24      two years ago, with the express purpose of

      25      diversifying the Nation's economy beyond gaming.





 

                                                                   20
       1             This decision was not made lightly.  Instead,

       2      it was backed up by significant resources.

       3             The Nation committed $28 million of capital

       4      in Seneca Holdings' first five years of operations.

       5             We have had a tremendous amount of success

       6      during Seneca Holdings' first two years.

       7             This success benefits, both, the Nation, and

       8      the entire Western New York region, a region that is

       9      sorely in need of economic development and capital

      10      investment.

      11             Starting with nothing, Seneca Holdings has

      12      built five successful operating subsidiaries and

      13      diverse industries, such as, construction,

      14      telecommunications, broadcasting, green energy, and

      15      others.

      16             All of these companies are based on

      17      Seneca Nation territories.  They are cutting-edge

      18      organizations, led by sophisticated business people.

      19             These companies have created millions of

      20      additional dollars in revenue, and jobs for both

      21      natives and non-native.

      22             In addition to our operating subsidiaries, we

      23      have invested significant capital in other promising

      24      businesses, most of which are located in

      25      Western New York.





 

                                                                   21
       1             We are investing in the region, with a

       2      purpose of building companies and revenues, and

       3      returns for the Seneca Nation and our people.

       4             We invest in Western New York because it has

       5      been our home for over 1,000 years.

       6             We will always be here.

       7             We are truly committed to the region like no

       8      other.  And unlike multi-national companies that

       9      come and go through the region and the state, we

      10      will not relocate, and our expanding dollars stay

      11      here.

      12             During my first two years, after coming back

      13      to the Seneca Nation, and helping to build

      14      Seneca Holdings, one thing has become apparent:  The

      15      Western New York business community wants to build

      16      Western New York's economy alongside the

      17      Seneca Nation.

      18             This community understands that a rising tide

      19      lifts all boats, and that the Seneca Nation can be a

      20      strong and valuable tidal catalyst.

      21             For example:  The Seneca Nation and its

      22      companies have valuable and unique business

      23      advantages, particularly in the federal sector.

      24             Seneca Holdings is targeting federal

      25      contracting work, and one of our subsidiaries is





 

                                                                   22
       1      closing in on a significant federal contract.

       2      However, we can't do all this work alone.

       3             Our strategy is to partner with our

       4      businesses, preferably in the Western New York

       5      region, to help us to complete this work, and expand

       6      our operations.

       7             This is truly a win-win, the Seneca Nation

       8      and our neighbors.

       9             The Seneca Nation businesses also have unique

      10      access to certain federal lending initiatives

      11      targeting Indian country.  We have already utilized

      12      these initiatives to help to build our company.

      13             In an environment of tight credit, these

      14      programs are incredibly valuable for our companies,

      15      and our partners.

      16             The Seneca Nation and Seneca Holdings are

      17      quickly becoming an economic, diversification

      18      success story.  Through Seneca Holdings, we are

      19      expanding our success beyond gaming and tobacco,

      20      into mainstream industries.  Again, this benefits

      21      everyone.

      22             The Western New York business community is

      23      beginning to understand the unique attributes that

      24      the Seneca Nation and its businesses bring to the

      25      table.





 

                                                                   23
       1             When I meet with Western New York business

       2      leaders, which is often, they're excited to get

       3      involved, and work together, to build the regional

       4      economy.  They want the tide to rise.

       5             And, they understand that the Seneca Nation

       6      represents one of the best ways to accomplish this.

       7             Thank you for your time.

       8             SENATOR MAZIARZ:  Thank you very much,

       9      Chairman Nephew, and Mr. Kimelberg.

      10             Again, we appreciate you being here.

      11             Just, if you could -- Richard, my area of

      12      questioning is in the area of Kinzua Dam.

      13             And, could you just explain to us, where the

      14      Nation is, at this time, with that development?

      15             I know that I have appeared at hearings,

      16      along with the Senecas.  I think it's a great

      17      opportunity for Western New York; for the

      18      Southern Tier of Western New York, and also for the

      19      Seneca Nation.

      20             Could you would just brief us on where we're

      21      at with that?

      22             RICHARD NEPHEW:  Okay, to give you a short

      23      history first, and then what we had hoped to do.

      24             It goes back many years, I believe, to at

      25      least the 1940s, where there was an interest in





 

                                                                   24
       1      building a dam, ostensibly, for flood control.

       2             That's the story that we had back in the eras

       3      of the '40s and '50s.

       4             We didn't know, at the time, it was never

       5      explained to us, that it was also about generating

       6      electricity.

       7             There were some very murky perspectives on

       8      that, but, nonetheless, the dam was built.  And,

       9      resulting in the flooding of approximately
